what: The heuristic parses propositional facts to identify the depot, customers, and the variable/value pairs for loc and visited. In new(), it precomputes a directed distance matrix from grounded visit/return/visit-via-depot operator costs, sorted nearest-customer lists for every place, customer demands, capacity, vehicle limit, and a fallback penalty. In compute_heuristic(), it reads the current location, load, vehicle count, and unvisited set, then greedily constructs a nearest-neighbor CVRP plan: it continues the current route when capacity allows, starts a new route via the depot when needed and allowed, and finally adds the return-to-depot cost.
why: CVRP remaining cost is dominated by routing distance and tight capacity/vehicle constraints. A sequential nearest-neighbor construction with exact operator costs is fast, generalizes across instances, and gives a non-admissible but usually close upper bound on remaining cost, which helps guide search with few expansions. Using exact operator costs avoids fragile parsing of derived numeric names, and optional capacity/demand/max-vehicles inputs degrade permissively if the translator folds them.
